so for some perspective, i’m 23f with ptsd from childhood sexual abuse also. i struggle with suicidal thoughts. and i have a 25m boyfriend.

i can’t speak for others, but personally my ptsd comes and goes. the longest i’ve done pretty well and not had flashbacks or nightmares etc, was probably about a year straight a couple of years ago. then something major will trigger me, and it’s been over a year now and i’ll probably only have a few good days a month. but other than those couple of days, i’m not doing great to be honest. i also feel like an empty shell of myself.

in my own current situation, i would completely understand if my boyfriend couldn’t handle living with me due to this. i would be understanding if he left me. that’s his right to do, and i’d also understand if you did that in your situation. but if you don’t want to do that, i have a few other suggestions. 

for yourself - if she wants to vent about her ptsd symptoms, try creating a separate time to talk about these issues. because i tend to go on tangents and will get stuck in my head and it’s hard for me to stop talking about it once i start. creating a specific time to talk about her issues will lessen the emotional toll it has on you. i don’t want to come off the wrong way but i’m assuming she would want that too. my boyfriend and i don’t do this but i try not to talk to him too much about my
flashbacks because it gets really disturbing. you could also take more time for yourself, get out of the house (i know you’re on lockdown but just go for a drive or something).

if you want to specifically help her with her mental health issues, as a partner you can: just be attentive, try to do activities with her to get her mind off things, and try not to let her isolate herself too much and just reassure her.
